definition: A device purchase subsidy deducted once from the factory price at activation. Receiving it creates a baseline plan commitment.
An extra subsidy paid by the dealer on top of the public subsidy. Its cap is a ratio of the public subsidy.
The lowest monthly plan level a customer must keep during the commitment period. Going below it creates a difference penalty.
The commitment of a public-subsidy customer to keep a plan at or above the baseline for a fixed period from activation.
The amount reclaimed when a customer goes below the baseline within the commitment period: the subsidy difference times the remaining-period ratio.
An exception that waives the difference penalty when verified seniors or welfare recipients switch to a designated plan, even within the commitment period.
An exception that pauses the commitment clock while a line is suspended for active-duty service.
A contract that discounts the monthly fee by a fixed rate instead of paying a public subsidy. The rate lives on the rules page.
The sum of device principal and plan fees over the contract. It is the basis for comparing the public subsidy with the selective contract.
